text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: synth-probe 'probe-heartbeat-eu-west' fired (P1). 18/20 recent heartbeats failed in last 5m. Symptoms: 503 responses from prober service. PD incident: https://pd.example/incidents/PD12345 - auto-page to #incidents.
oncall-alex: Acked. I'm on it. Pulling recent deploys + probe config.
maria-sre: Noted. I'm available to jump in if this looks like prober throttling. Any config rollouts in last 30m?
jamie-eng: I saw a rolling update to the routing layer ~12m ago that added a new rate-limiter flag for health-check paths. Tagging @maria-sre and @oncall-alex.
oncall-alex: Checking prober logs now. Running: 
```
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" https://synth-prober-eu-west.internal/heartbeat
```
Got repeated: `503 0.145` and `timeout` from a subset of prober workers.
ops-bot: Auto-suppression rule triggered: synth-probe-heartbeat-suppression for service prober-scheduler (suppression_id: sup-87). Suppression started at 2356788900 and has a 10m default window.
samantha-support: Customer impact check: no active customer incidents in intercom yet, but a customer-facing dashboard uses these probes for uptime display. If probes stay failing, it will show degraded status.
maria-sre: That suppression looks suspicious — it may have been auto-applied because the scheduler hit a transient error. If suppression is active probes won't fanout to all regions. Can we un-suppress?
jamie-eng: I'll try to lift suppression and restart the prober worker pool on eu-west. Executing: `kubectl -n prober rollout restart deploy/prober-worker-eu-west`
oncall-alex: Before restart, I'm going to remove the suppression so we can see live behavior: `opsctl suppression remove sup-87 --force`
ops-bot: Suppression sup-87 removed by oncall-alex at 2356789028.
jamie-eng: Restart issued. Watching logs...
```
kubectl logs -n prober deploy/prober-worker-eu-west --tail=50
```
Now seeing steady 200s from restarted pods.
PD-oncall: PD incident acknowledged by pd-oncall at 2356789032. Escalation to SRE after 5m if not acked.
samantha-support: Posting proactive note to status page draft: "Investigating synthetic probe failures in EU-West. Internal teams are investigating; no confirmed customer-facing outages yet." Will post if we see persistent failures.
maria-sre: Good. Also checking runway: metrics show spike in prober CPU around time of routing change. Could be rate-limiter mis-tagging health-check path as user traffic. Jamie, can you revert the rate-limiter flag or add exception for /heartbeat?
jamie-eng: Rolling back the rate-limiter change for health-checks now. Patch: `git revert 9f2cbe` -> redeploying routing service.
oncall-alex: After restart + suppression removal, probes are reporting mixed but trending green. 60/60 checks across regions: eu-west showing 98% pass in last 3m.
ops-bot: Synthetic probe polling resumed full fanout at 2356789055.
PD-oncall: Marking PD incident PD12345 as under investigation (ack).
samantha-support: Status page update posted: "Mitigated — probes recovered in EU-West; monitoring. We're investigating root cause (routing rule change and suppression interplay)."
maria-sre: Creating incident ticket IN-7890 with initial postmortem stub. Assigning to jamie-eng as primary and maria-sre as SRE lead.
jamie-eng: I'll follow up with a remediation plan: (1) ensure suppression rules require human approval for critical synth probes, (2) add explicit rate-limiter allowlist for health-check paths, (3) add extra alerting to detect suppression-induced fanout reduction.
oncall-alex: Handoff to maria-sre for deeper RCA. I'm clear to hand off; returning to standby.
maria-sre: Taking command for RCA and follow-ups. PD oncall, please leave incident open until postmortem draft ready.
PD-oncall: Will keep the PD incident open and update timelines. Logging timeline and tags.
samantha-support: I'll close the status page note once the postmortem is published.
ops-bot: Automated follow-up: schedule postmortem meeting in 24h (calendar invite sent to jamie-eng, maria-sre, oncall-alex, samantha-support).
maria-sre: Quick summary for the thread: root cause appears to be an interaction between a routing rate-limit feature and an auto-suppression rule that suppressed probe fanout; combined they caused a reduction in heartbeat coverage and triggered PagerDuty. Impact: temporary probe visibility degradation for EU-West, no confirmed customer traffic outage. Next actions: postmortem, suppression-policy change, routing allowlist, and additional monitors.
jamie-eng: Closing loop: verified probes stable for 10m, rolling back problematic flag, patch queued for code review.
oncall-alex: Thanks all — closing thread here after 30m of stable green. If anything regresses, re-open PD incident and ping #incidents. :white_check_mark:
